summary: Iteration 1 validated that simulated annealing (SA) with single-edge moves scores 89.5/100 on the rectangle packing problem, far above the greedy-only baseline of 20.3/100. The SA approach works by proposing valid edge expansions/contractions using precomputed per-edge bounds, achieving high acceptance rates. The next iteration should explore improved initialization (e.g., BSP/Voronoi partitioning) and SA move enhancements to push beyond 90.
key_points: SA with per-edge expansion bounds scored 89.5, confirming the hypothesis (predicted >85). Greedy-only scored 20.3, confirming the negative control (predicted 15-30).

Key insight: precomputing max expansion per edge direction (O(N) per edge) eliminates invalid SA proposals, dramatically improving iteration quality vs. random-step-then-reject approaches. Coordinated neighbor moves were too expensive and were dropped.

Remaining score gap (~10 points) likely comes from suboptimal initial placement (greedy cell-by-cell expansion is slow) and SA getting stuck in local optima. Next iteration should test: (1) BSP or power-diagram initialization for better starting rectangles, (2) multi-edge SA moves (grow width while shrinking height), (3) temperature schedule tuning, and (4) rectangle swap moves between adjacent companies.
